notes: Intro: Glint builds an in-editor copilot focused on buffering-free keystroke completions — tiny snippet suggestions, multi-line refactors, docstring synthesis.
Primary ask: consistent low-latency streaming for per-keystroke completions. TTFT (time-to-first-token) is a hard requirement for UX: target <80ms cold, <20ms hot (cached session).
They observed jitter spikes during internal tests when model fallback triggered — causes visible cursor jumps for users. Want metrics + SLO for jitter and P99 latency.
Token budget model: want per-session token caps and per-completion soft budgets. Expect token-aware backpressure: degrade completion length before dropping to a smaller model.
Model/version pinning: require pin by commit/hash + ability to route new sessions to canary model. Must be able to revert to deterministic older weights within 10m.
Streaming behavior needs to support per-character streaming and partial candidates; they will run sanity evals to measure TTFT & first-meaningful-token frequency.
Security: SSO + audit logs required for enterprise customers. Data residency: EU customers need region pinning for sessions. Priya pushed KMS integration scoping.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-18): "If the first suggestion isn't near-instant, users feel the assistant is laggy — TTFT is the UX."
POC scope agreed: three profiles — tiny completions (1-30 tokens), medium refactors (30-150 tokens), completion streaming under heavy parallel typing (backpressure test).
Success metrics: TTFT median/hot/cold, P95 completion latency, jitter (ms variance) during 1k concurrent edit sessions, token cost per 1k suggestions.
Current stack: VS Code extension + websocket relay -> internal proxy. They want to replace proxy with Redwood routing to test batching and KV cache for session warming.
Engineering notes: prefer hosted_api initially for speed of integration; evaluate Dedicated if we can't meet deterministic TTFT or for EU residency.
Asked for: micro-benchmark template + suggested token budget heuristics, backpressure strategies (truncate, model-fallback, or micro-completions), and recommended streaming chunk size (8-16 tokens).
Concerns: saw degraded throughput when kernel selection changed during autoscaling. Want docs on kernel/quantization profiles and how they affect cold TTFT.
Next-touch: schedule POC kickoff, share Fireflies transcript and POC benchmark sheet, get Redwood SE to instrument first-meaningful-token telemetry.
Short-hand CRM entry: POC greenfield — focus TTFT/jitter/backpressure. AE to confirm access to EU region account for residency tests.
